Important Update About Our Practice : 

Acumed Veterinary Specialty will now become an exclusive Neurology Practice, the OPD / General Practice will close down soon. 

After 12 years of caring for your companions, we are writing to share that Acumed's OPD / General Practice will be closing. As Dr. Prathmesh Deshmukh has taken on a new role and will be partially moving to a different city, we can no longer assure the same-day or next-day availability that general practice requires. After much thought, we have taken this difficult decision.

Importantly, we are not closing entirely. Acumed will continue as an exclusive Referral Neurology Clinic, seeing neurology cases by referral on a few days each month.

We will not stop all at once. To help you transition, we are staggering the wind-down: services will reduce through July, continue on limited days until mid-August 2026, and our ongoing acupuncture patients can visit on select days until September 2026.

For routine care, we recommend a trusted vet close to your home. We're happy to help — write to us with your location for suggestions.

Thank you for placing your trust in us. This has been a difficult decision for us too.

Since 2014, it has been our privilege and joy to care for your beloved companions. We are deeply grateful to every pet parent who has walked through our doors and trusted us with the health and wellbeing of their furry family members. Thank you for being a part of our journey.

We have been gradually refining the scope of our practice and reducing the range of general services at our clinic. This has been a thoughtful and ongoing process, and we are now ready to take the next step.

Acumed Veterinary Specialty is transitioning into an exclusive referral neurology practice. Our Out-Patient Department (OPD) and General Practice consultations will be gradually wound down and will cease in the coming months.

Going forward, we will be accepting cases exclusively through veterinary referrals for neurological consultations, diagnostics, and advanced neurology care.
If you have been visiting us for general or routine consultations, we kindly encourage you to connect with a trusted general practice veterinarian in your neighborhood for your pet's ongoing primary care needs. We are happy to help with recommendations if needed.

During this transition over the next few months, our working days may be fewer than usual, and there may be occasional clinic closures that we may not always be able to announce in advance. We truly appreciate your understanding and patience, and we sincerely apologize for any inconvenience.

Updated : May 2026.

featured_reviews.name: vikas nalawade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review about a stray cat named “Leopard” who eventually became our family member. Request you to please read it till end, as it may be helpful to any pet parent.
Leopard met with an accident and was missing for a week’s period. Later we found him & we noticed that he had a fracture at shoulder of right forelimb. Doctors told us that leg needs to be operated by inserting rod in his leg, so we got him operated by Dr. Sunetra. The surgery went well, but three days after surgery, Leopard's operated leg started swelling, we informed Dr. Sunetra but she told us it is the swelling due to surgery and it will subside downwards. But that swelling was due to infection and it lead to pus formation. Next day the swelling increased and in the evening pus started oozing out, seeing this we called up Dr. Sunetra & rushed to her with our Leopard. Dr. told us to keep flushing the wound twice a day with betadine. After 2-3 days of this treatment, the skin around the infected area went dead and we had a clear sight of his wound with operated area, where we could see his bone from two points because healing was not completed & the stitches were opened. We even asked Dr. Sunetra the doubt in our mind that this infection will not spread in his operated leg & internal body, to which she responded, it would not.
Eventually his external pain reduced but he had internal pain, which we failed to understand. He could not tolerate the pain and stopped eating and got fever exactly on 8th day from operation. I heard about Dr. Pethe's Clinic when I had lost all hope.
Muthu was diagnosed of Acute Kidney Failure (creatinine 14.1) and my regular Vet was unable to do anything - that is when I visited the Pethes for a second opinion.
The Clinic is a very simple set up. But the people who take care of the place are Excellent!
Right from the very first day, when I watched how they were able to get Muthu's X-rays, and how they would literally treat him at his comfort level (meaning, they could tell that he was anxious and did their best to calm him - in fact, many times, they were on the floor when they had to give him an injection).
As a result of their never-giving-up-attitude, Muthu's creatine level dropped to 2.1 (in 3 months). For me, those 3 months were God-given days to cherish. Even though he was on medicines every day, even though we had to keep him on a strict diet and make regular visits to the Clinic, I am ever grateful to God for those 3 months. And, a huge reason for this are Dr. & Mrs. Pethe and all their staff.
Dogs can sense hospitals. Muthu would usually throw a tantrum whenever we approached the "super speciality pet hospital" which we were so accustomed to before we met the Pethes. But ever since we started going to Pethe's Clinic, Muthu became cooperative. I am sure the procedure was not easy on him either. But, he could tell that the people attending to him cared for him. You see, animals can tell by the touch - by the way we approach them. And Muthu was able to cooperate only because of the friendly and caring nature demonstrated by all the staff (Shinu, Ajay, and the others). They would give him biscuits, play with him, and make him feel comfortable. They didn't need people holding him down whenever they gave him bottles of saline (which would often last for 1.2 hours).
But even as Muthu's creatinine levels decreased, Dr & Mrs. Pethe were honest with me about his condition. And they did it with utmost care, concern, and compassion. They let me know that kidney failure could not be reversed.
After nearly 3.5 months of treatment, Muthu's condition began to worsen. And even during our last visit to the Clinic, Mrs. Pethe brought a 2 month pup near Muthu to make him smile.
It's been 6 months since I have lost my friend Muthu. And all pet lovers will know that it is not easy.
But, I am so glad to have met the Pethes who cared for him and helped me through those days.
Both Dr. & Mrs. Pethe are geniuses in their own way of knowledge and expertise.  But, what makes them stand out from the rest is their human touch and their genuine love and care for animals.
God bless the Team at Pethe's Clinic.

Review for Pet Clinic Gorai – Dr. Premal Darji

I am writing this with extreme pain after losing my beloved pet, Erika.

I was referred to Pet Clinic Gorai and trusted Dr. Premal Darji completely. That trust has turned into lifelong regret.

Erika had a tumor case, and instead of receiving clear surgical direction and decisive medical planning, her treatment kept getting prolonged with medications. During this period, her condition worsened, and she started experiencing severe bleeding episodes.

We repeatedly requested clarity about surgical intervention and long-term treatment planning. However, we never received firm guidance or urgency that such a critical case required.

At one stage, her platelet levels dropped significantly, and her bleeding became uncontrollable. Watching your pet lose blood helplessly while depending on professional guidance is something no pet parent should ever experience. Despite multiple visits and continuous follow-ups, her condition deteriorated rapidly.

We were left confused, emotionally shattered, and without clear answers.

If you are dealing with a serious or tumor-related condition, please:
– Ask for detailed blood reports and explanations
– Ask about platelet monitoring
– Seek immediate second opinions
– Do not delay critical decisions

Blind trust in medical situations can cost you everything. In our case, it cost us our family member.

The pain my family is going through cannot be described in words. Losing Erika has left a permanent void in our lives.

I hope no other pet parent has to go through this trauma.

featured_reviews.name: Jonita Quadras
featured_reviews.review_text:
We rescued our cat, Kiki, on January 29th 2025. A couple of weeks in, we suspected she might be pregnant and took her to Dr. Premal Darji. He strongly advised immediate spaying, assuring us it was completely safe and routine. Trusting his judgment, we went ahead with the surgery.

Soon after, Kiki began vomiting excessively — far more than what he described as “normal.” She stopped eating, peeing, or pooping. We visited his clinic daily post-op, but Dr. Darji had no clear answers. At one point, he even said he hadn’t “seen a case like this before,” but never recommended a specialist or second opinion.

Eventually, when we visited another vet, bloodwork revealed that Kiki’s creatinine was dangerously high (15) — a clear sign of acute kidney failure. We went back to Dr. Darji for an ultrasound, but again he insisted that “everything looked fine,” and failed to identify the actual issue. Even then, he didn’t show any urgency or transparency in managing the situation.

Desperate for help, we rushed her to Top Dog Clinic in Andheri, where they quickly diagnosed that urine was leaking into her abdomen, most likely due to trauma caused during the original spay surgery. They couldn’t keep her overnight, so we stabilized her at Blue 7 Vets in Borivali, and the next day, Top Dog performed a critical, life-saving surgery.

Kiki thankfully made it through, and while she still has one more surgery to go, she’s finally recovering. What’s most upsetting is that none of this had to happen. Dr. Darji never took accountability or gave us the information we needed to act sooner. His lack of proper communication and judgment not only endangered Kiki’s life but also left us emotionally drained and over ₹2 lakhs deep in treatment costs that could have been avoided.

This isn’t to spread hate, but to create awareness. If you feel unsure or uncomfortable with your vet’s advice, please don’t hesitate to seek a second opinion. Your pet’s life and your peace of mind are worth it.

January in Numbers 🏥🐾
Every number tells a story of care, commitment, and compassion.
From emergency responses to successful treatments, January reflected the impact of dedicated veterinary care at Utkarsh Animal Hospital.
Because for us, metrics aren’t just numbers — they’re lives touched and lives saved.

जानेवारीचे आकडे 🏥🐾
प्रत्येक आकडा सांगतो सेवा, समर्पण आणि करुणेची गोष्ट.
आपत्कालीन मदत असो किंवा यशस्वी उपचार — जानेवारी महिना उत्कर्ष अ‍ॅनिमल हॉस्पिटलमधील विश्वासार्ह पशुवैद्यकीय सेवेचा ठसा उमटवणारा ठरला.
आमच्यासाठी आकडे म्हणजे फक्त संख्या नाहीत — ती वाचवलेली आयुष्ये आहेत.

Animals have rights too—and it is our responsibility to know and uphold them.
Animal welfare laws are designed to protect animals from cruelty, neglect, and abuse, ensuring they live with dignity and care. When we are informed about these laws, we become stronger voices for those who cannot speak for themselves.

Know a few important animal welfare rules in India:
• Causing cruelty, injury, or abandonment of animals is a punishable offence under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960.
• Feeding or caring for community animals is legal and protected.
• Injured or sick animals must be given timely medical care.
• Animals have the right to food, water, shelter, and freedom from pain and fear.

Being aware is the first step towards action. Let’s stand together as responsible citizens and create a safer, more compassionate society for all living beings.

प्राण्यांनाही हक्क आहेत—आणि ते जाणून घेणे व त्यांचे संरक्षण करणे ही आपली जबाबदारी आहे.
प्राणी कल्याण कायदे प्राण्यांना क्रूरता, दुर्लक्ष आणि छळापासून वाचवण्यासाठी तयार करण्यात आले आहेत, जेणेकरून त्यांना सन्मानाने व सुरक्षिततेने जीवन जगता येईल.

भारतामधील काही महत्त्वाचे प्राणी कल्याण नियम:
• प्राण्यांवर क्रूरता करणे, त्यांना दुखापत करणे किंवा सोडून देणे हे प्राणी क्रूरता प्रतिबंधक कायदा, 1960 अंतर्गत गुन्हा आहे.
• रस्त्यावरील किंवा सामुदायिक प्राण्यांना अन्न देणे व काळजी घेणे कायदेशीर आहे.
• जखमी किंवा आजारी प्राण्यांना त्वरित वैद्यकीय उपचार देणे आवश्यक आहे.

Animal Birth Control isn’t just about animals—it’s about creating healthier communities and ensuring humane, long-term care.
ABC programs help control stray populations ethically, reduce conflicts, prevent the spread of diseases, and improve the quality of life for both animals and people.
Responsible, compassionate solutions begin with awareness and action.

प्राणी जन्मनियंत्रण (ABC) हे केवळ प्राण्यांपुरते मर्यादित नाही—ते निरोगी समाज आणि मानवी दृष्टिकोनातून काळजी घेण्याबाबत आहे.
ABC कार्यक्रमांमुळे भटक्या प्राण्यांची संख्या नैतिक पद्धतीने नियंत्रणात राहते, आजारांचा प्रसार कमी होतो, संघर्ष टाळले जातात आणि माणसे व प्राणी दोघांचेही जीवनमान सुधारते.
जबाबदार आणि करुणामय उपाययोजना जागरूकतेपासून आणि कृतीपासून सुरू होतात.

एनिमल बर्थ कंट्रोल (ABC) सिर्फ जानवरों के बारे में नहीं है—यह स्वस्थ समुदाय और मानवीय देखभाल सुनिश्चित करने का एक ज़रूरी कदम है।
ABC कार्यक्रम नैतिक तरीके से आवारा जानवरों की संख्या नियंत्रित करते हैं, बीमारियों के खतरे को कम करते हैं, टकराव रोकते हैं और इंसानों व जानवरों दोनों के जीवन स्तर को बेहतर बनाते हैं।
जिम्मेदार और संवेदनशील समाधान जागरूकता और सही कदमों से शुरू होते हैं।

True freedom lies in compassion—for people, animals, and our nation.
Celebrating a Republic that cares for all.

खरे स्वातंत्र्य करुणेत आहे—माणसांसाठी, प्राण्यांसाठी आणि आपल्या राष्ट्रासाठी.
सर्वांची काळजी घेणाऱ्या प्रजासत्ताकाचा आज गौरव साजरा करूया.

सच्ची आज़ादी करुणा में निहित है—लोगों के लिए, पशुओं के लिए और हमारे राष्ट्र के लिए।
ऐसे गणराज्य का उत्सव मनाएँ जो सबकी परवाह करता है।

featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst experience.💔

I rescued a severely injured stray cat who was left to die on the road. One of his legs was badly damaged, and with genuine intention to save his life, I brought him here hoping he would receive proper treatment.

Instead of focusing on immediate care or suggesting alternate support options, I was asked to pay ₹5,000–₹6,000 upfront, while being told the total treatment could cost around ₹22,000. As someone who tried to help purely on humanitarian grounds, this was extremely discouraging.

I clearly explained my financial situation and honestly said that I could manage only ₹600–₹700 from my side, which was my genuine capacity. Unfortunately, there was no flexibility, no discussion about raising donations through their network, social media, or other sponsors — which I believe NGOs usually do.

If NGOs start asking large amounts from people who rescue and bring injured strays, then many good-hearted people will stop helping animals altogether. This defeats the very purpose of animal welfare.

With a heavy heart, I had no option but to leave the cat there, feeling helpless and guilty, knowing he might continue to suffer.

This experience was emotionally distressing and disappointing.

At the time of surgery, required injectable medications were administered as per protocol, and possible post-operative effects, expected recovery signs, and precautions were clearly explained to the owners. This is also reflected in the signed consent form, which explicitly states that post-operative care is the owner’s responsibility and that complications can arise if proper care is not followed.

Multiple follow-up calls were received and attended, during which the owners were advised to bring the cat back to the clinic for evaluation and required care. Additionally, the owners were specifically asked to visit the clinic the very same to collect the required post-operative medications, which they did not comply with.

Post-operative recovery can be compromised if wound care instructions are not followed. In this case, concern was repeatedly expressed about the cat cleaning itself, while basic precautions for protecting the suture site were resisted, and discomfort was shown toward necessary post-operative measures.

We would like to highlight that our clinic actively supports low-cost sterilization for rescued and stray animals, as a social service for caretakers who wish to help but may have financial constraints. We remain open to constructive dialogue and encourage pet parents to return to the clinic when advised, as post-operative outcomes depend on shared responsibility between the veterinarian and the caretaker.

Accordingly, the standard medical approach is to first stabilize the patient with intravenous fluids and supportive care before proceeding with definitive procedures.

Appropriate treatment was initiated, including fluid therapy, painkillers and attempts to relieve the obstruction. A significant amount of urethral debris was removed; however, the obstruction could not be completely relieved at that stage without increasing procedural risk. Further intervention under controlled conditions was advised once the patient’s status improved.

You were informed about the critical nature of the condition, the guarded prognosis, and the need for urgent follow-up. featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a terrible and traumatic experience at Indira Pets Clinic & Care Center with my dog, who was clearly choking on a bone. Despite telling the receptionist it was an emergency, I was made to wait in the regular queue for almost two hours while my dog struggled and I was panicking. The staff showed no urgency, compassion, or basic understanding of how serious choking can be.
When we were finally called in, the doctor barely examined my dog and said there was “nothing in her throat,” even though I could clearly feel something stuck. Instead of properly investigating or attempting to address the obstruction, he gave my dog three injections without clearly explaining what they were or how they would help in a choking situation. There was no effort to reassure me or to treat the case as an emergency.
I was so unhappy and worried that I rushed my dog to another vet clinic. There, the vet immediately took my dog in, gave prompt attention, and administered an oral medicine that actually helped the stuck piece move down. My dog improved quickly after that, proving that something really was wrong and that the first clinic had failed to act appropriately.
This was one of the worst veterinary experiences I have ever had. The lack of empathy, poor triage, and dismissive attitude at Indira Pets Clinic & Care Center put my dog at risk and caused me immense stress. I will never take my pet there again and do not recommend this clinic to anyone who expects genuine emergency care or basic professionalism for their animals.

I visited this place last week and google maps is showing another route i.e from goregaon check naka till arey colony bus then 15mins walk from there. However there is a gate on the highway itself. I visited the place 3days before getting my pet due to this location issue.

I seen a door in the inside common area but it was open.
I had luckily carried a cone so i used that.

Consultation was Rs.200 and Online payments are accepted however I recommend to carry cash as online was not working. They give a receipt which you have to carry the next time you visit .

Apart from that I may have to visit again after 10days so will update. (Edit)
I visited 2-3times after that and was recommended not to do blood test. My cat's fungal infection went only thing is the hair did not grow back hence i went for a 4th visit, i also got blood test done and the report came on my WhatsApp number same day by night.
